hero: Opens with a custom WebGL scene behind a spare header line: 'Jordan Delcros — Creative Developer — Freelance'. A branded page loader with an intro animation runs first and doubles as a gate to 'unlock' sound. Credibility in the first 5s is the graphics engineering itself — a live 3D/generative canvas and gesture interaction — rather than copy or logos. This is the ANTI-REFERENCE: the signature graphic is loud and near-immersive, so editorial text is reduced to a single role line.
wordmark_identity: Name set as plain text ('Jordan Delcros'), not a stylized logotype or monogram — the WebGL graphic, not the type, carries identity. The generative visual is effectively the brand mark. Restraint is inverted vs. an editorial site: the type stays neutral precisely because the moving graphic is doing the identity work.
signature_detail: The ownable element is the WebGL/generative system: a canvas-based 3D scene with gesture/pointer-reactive interaction, hidden interactive items scattered through the experience, and a sound layer unlocked at load. Jury singled out 'main user interaction' and animations (~8.0/10) as the standout. This is the calibration point — the signature graphic is pushed almost to overwhelming, sacrificing editorial calm and a11y (dev/accessibility scored lowest, ~6.4/10) for spectacle.
typography: Sans-serif, minimal and neutral — type is deliberately quiet so the WebGL dominates. Small role/label text rather than a big editorial display scale; no serif pairing or optical-sizing devices observed. Letterforms function as UI captions over the 3D scene rather than as the main visual. Exact typeface undisclosed. [uncertain]
whitespace_layout: Layout is experience-led, not grid-led: an 'unusual navigation' with content revealed through interaction and hidden items rather than a conventional scrolling column. Negative space is filled by the live canvas rather than empty margin, so 'designed' here reads as spatial/3D composition instead of vertical editorial rhythm. [uncertain]
color_accent_discipline: Very restrained palette anchored on a single light lavender-gray (#C7CEDC) as the dominant field, letting the WebGL lighting/motion supply visual interest instead of color. Effectively a near-monochrome cool-gray base with the 3D render providing highlights — accent discipline is achieved by desaturation so the moving graphic isn't fighting bright color.
light_dark_tone: Reads as a single cool light-lavender-gray tone rather than a light/dark toggle; no dual-theme system documented. The muted #C7CEDC base is what keeps the loud WebGL from becoming garish. [uncertain]
motion: Motion-maximal: custom intro loader animation, continuous WebGL/generative rendering, gesture- and pointer-driven interaction, and animated transitions between sections (jury animations ~8.0/10, creativity ~8.22/10, its highest axis). Easing is fluid and interaction-reactive. This is the far end of the spectrum — motion is nearly always on-screen, the opposite of transform/opacity restraint.
reduced_motion_a11y: Weak point and the cautionary lesson: 'Accessibility in development' was the lowest jury axis (~6.40/10). No documented prefers-reduced-motion static fallback; the sound-unlock loader and gesture navigation add interaction cost. Continuous WebGL + hidden/gesture nav work against keyboard and reduced-motion users — exactly the trade-off to avoid for a clinical-credibility brand. [uncertain]
project_presentation: Curated 'top projects' surfaced inside the interactive/3D experience rather than a flat card grid, with hidden interactive items revealing work as you explore. Depth is delivered experientially; conventional per-project artifact density (repos, screenshots, spec text) is de-emphasized in favor of the guided motion journey. [uncertain]
research_artifact_presentation: No academic papers/talks surface. His engineering credibility lives off-site on GitHub (OBJImg — 3D-model-to-compressed-image for THREE.js, the 'Jo' framework) and CodePen rather than as on-page citations or model cards. [uncertain]
writing_blog_integration: No blog/essay index fused into the portfolio; it is a pure showcase experience. Technical output is expressed as open-source repos and CodePen demos externally, not an on-site writing feed. [uncertain]
photography_imagery: Little to no personal/editorial photography — imagery is generated by the WebGL renderer, not shot media. Visuals are procedural/real-time rather than a photo library, so 'imagery' and 'signature graphic' are the same layer here.
navigation: Deliberately 'unusual navigation' — gesture/interaction-driven and non-linear rather than a sticky top bar with ordered links. Name sits as a neutral header line; discovery is exploratory, which is memorable but raises findability/a11y cost. [uncertain]
trust_credibility: Credibility signaled through the craft itself (award recognition — Awwwards SOTD, Muzli Pick) plus off-site GitHub/CodePen presence, rather than client logos or affiliation rows in the hero. The work quality is the trust marker. [uncertain]
contact_conversion: Portfolio invites visitors to discover projects and get in touch for work as a freelancer; contact is a light 'reach out' path surfaced within the experience rather than a prominent Cal.com/booking CTA. Conversion is soft, subordinate to the showcase. [uncertain]
performance_weight: Heavier by nature: continuous WebGL/Three.js rendering, custom loader, shaders and audio assets. WPO/responsive were not the standout scores and accessibility-in-dev was lowest — page weight and GPU cost are real. Uses THREE.js with author's own optimizations (e.g. OBJImg compressing 3D models to images) to fight asset weight, but the motion budget is large. [uncertain]
takeaway: STEAL: the desaturation discipline — pairing a loud generative graphic with a single muted base (#C7CEDC) so the signature never turns garish, exactly the guardrail for keeping an ECG/WebGL flourish subordinate to maroon editorial calm. AVOID: letting the signature graphic become the whole site — gesture-only 'unusual navigation', a sound-gated loader, and always-on WebGL tanked accessibility (~6.4/10) and buried the work; for a clinical+technical brand, cap the generative element to one restrained, reduced-motion-aware moment and keep navigation conventional and legible.
